chunks: And his story with Hababa al-Walibiyya, the owner of the pebble on which Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) placed his seal,
and he said to her: 'One who places a seal on this is an Imam.'
And she remained until the days of al-Rida (peace be upon him), and he placed his seal on it,
and she witnessed the placing of seals by those of his ancestors who preceded him (peace be upon them), and they placed their seals on it,
and he (peace be upon him) was the last of them whom she met, and she died after meeting him, and he shrouded her in his shirt.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin (Commander of the Faithful), a title for Imam Ali
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida, referring to Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْحِصَاة: The pebble or stone used as a seal/token
key_terms.حَبَابَةَ الْوَالِبِيَّةِ: Hababa al-Walibiyya, the owner of the pebble
key_terms.طُبِعَ: He placed his seal (stamp/signet) upon it
key_terms.قَمِيصِهِ: His shirt, used as a shroud

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the pebble (al-hisah) associated with Hababa and the Imams?
ai.summary: This narrative from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the physical continuity of the Imamate through the 'pebble of authority' (al-Hisaa), serving as a tangible proof of succession (Nass) from Imam Ali to Imam al-Rida. The detail that Hababa witnessed the seals of the preceding Imams underscores the unbroken chain of divine designation, while her burial in the Imam’s shirt signifies the high honor accorded to those who bear witness to the Ahl al-Bayt’s authority. This tradition reinforces the Shia doctrine of the Imamate as a hereditary and divinely appointed institution, validated by both physical tokens and eyewitness testimony.
